source_text: Aut vi rapuerit aut calumniam fecerit. Rapina et fraus unum altare polluunt. Convertimini qui opprimitis.
thought_title: Violence and fraud defile the one altar
orientation: Origen is applying Leviticus 5:21 (6:2) to the soul, explaining that violence and fraud both defile the same altar of faith between brothers.
pass_a_gloss: Or if he has taken by force or has made false accusation. Robbery and fraud defile one altar. Be converted, you who oppress.

choices.why: Keeps the legal force of calumnia as a false charge, matching the sin context of Leviticus 5:21 (6:2).
Polluo is the standard term for ritual and moral defilement, continuing the altar imagery from the previous section.
The passive imperative carries the call to turn back to God, echoing the homily's theme of conversion.
Opprimo denotes crushing or oppressing others, fitting the context of violence and fraud against a neighbor.

bible_refs.note: The source continues the citation from the previous section: 'Aut vi rapuerit aut calumniam fecerit' echoes the offenses listed in Leviticus 5:21 (6:2) LXX.

pass_b_english: Or if someone has taken by force or made a false accusation. Robbery and fraud defile one and the same altar. Be converted, you who oppress.

last_rejected.why: English hides that this is Scripture quotation (imperative 'Convertimini' with prophetic force).
last_rejected.fix: Turn back, you who oppress—Scripture's direct address.
last_rejected.ruling: English accurately renders 'Convertimini qui opprimitis' as imperative; no meaning lost or changed.
